Synopsis:
Outcome dialog for the Iron throne. Major part with Ravengard thanking the player, explaining that the emperor extended their protection to Ravengard, and that Ravengard will wait for them in camp where they can talk again.

Cluster Contexts:
- IRN_IronThrone_Return.json: You’ve just come out of the Iron Throne encounter — the Throne has been neutralized and the hostages rescued — and the scene follows that immediate outcome. These events sit against the wider Steel Watch/Foundry crisis (the Neurocitor control centre and Watcher network) that drew you into the conflict, so the city remains tense even as the Throne falls. Ravengard appears grateful, reports that the emperor has formally extended protection to him, and tells you he will wait for you at camp so you can speak privately. That off‑screen promise of imperial protection signals official recognition and sets up further discussion and consequences back at camp.
- IRN_IronThrone_ReturnRavengard_OM_Wyll_AOM_OOM.json: Outcome dialog for the Iron throne. Wyll gets reunited with Ravengard and they have an OM discussion. Should also explain how Ravengard is now protected by the Emperor's protection and he will be in camp after this.
- IRN_IronThrone_ReturnRavengard_OM_Wyll_COM.json: Outcome dialog for the Iron throne. Wyll gets reunited with Ravengard and they have an OM discussion. Should also explain how Ravengard is now protected by the Emperor's protection and he will be in camp after this.
- IRN_IronThrone_ReturnHostages.json: Off‑screen you recently rescued Obelia Toobin from a prison explosion, leaving her Gondian leader (Zanner Toobin) relieved and desperate — the hostages were being used to control their families who work in the Steelwatch Foundry and force them to build Watchers and other weapons. The Foundry’s control centre is the Neurocitor, a Gondian–illithid neural switchboard on the lowest floor whose blended tech links and controls every Steel Watcher and is not easily destroyed by ordinary means; the intended way to disable it risks a cascading explosion. In this conversation Obelia thanks the player, begs them to go free the families at the Foundry (offering the quest if it hasn’t been given), and reacts differently depending on whether the player already knows about or has promised to help the Iron Throne hostages. Mechanically, if the player saves a majority of both the Iron Throne hostages and the Steelwatch Foundry hostages, the survivors will help by turning Steel Watchers to the player in the final battle; otherwise they offer only narrative thanks (and only a hint of reward if enough Iron Throne hostages survived).
- IRN_IronThrone_Destruction.json: The Iron Throne is seen collapsing under the water pressure. If players managed to escape, they are seen escaping with the submersible.

Dialogue Excerpts (up to 3 samples, ordered):
Sample 1:
- Narrator: *Calmness greets you as the submersible slows to a halt. Unlike the Iron Throne, you remain intact.* (node 21)
- Narrator: *So, it seems, will the families of all the hostages rescued from the Throne.* (node 9)
